subject: Maths
title: Factorising quadratics
subtitle: Quadratic Equations · GCSE Maths
learning_objective: I can factorise quadratic expressions of the form x² + bx + c and ax² + bx + c.

key_vocab.definition: Factorising a quadratic means writing it as a product of two brackets. For x² + bx + c, find two numbers that multiply to c and add to b.

sections.title: Learning Objective
sections.content: I can factorise quadratic expressions of the form x² + bx + c and ax² + bx + c.

sections.title: Key Words
sections.content: Factorising -- Factorising a quadratic means writing it as a product of two brackets. For x² + bx + c, find two numbers that multiply to c and add to b.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
Find two numbers that multiply to c and add to b, then write x² + bx + c = (x + m)(x + n).
x² + bx + c = (x + m)(x + n) where mn = c and m + n = b
Product = c, Sum = b

Key examples:
  ✓ x² + 7x + 12 = (x + 3)(x + 4)  (3 × 4 = 12, 3 + 4 = 7)
  ✓ x² − 5x + 6 = (x − 2)(x − 3)  (−2 × −3 = 6, −2 + −3 = −5)
  ✓ x² + x − 12 = (x + 4)(x − 3)  (4 × −3 = −12, 4 + −3 = 1)
  ✗ x² + 7x + 12 = (x + 6)(x + 2)  (6 + 2 = 8, not 7)
  ✗ x² − 5x + 6 = (x − 6)(x + 1)  (−6 × 1 = −6, not +6)

sections.title: Worked Example
sections.content:
Example 1 – both positive
  Factorise x² + 8x + 15
  Need two numbers: multiply to 15, add to 8
  Factor pairs of 15: 1×15, 3×5
  3 + 5 = 8, so (x + 3)(x + 5)
  (x + 3)(x + 5)
  (Both numbers positive because b and c are both positive.)

Example 2 – both negative
  Factorise x² − 7x + 12
  Need: multiply to +12, add to −7
  Both must be negative: −3 × −4 = 12, −3 + −4 = −7
  = (x − 3)(x − 4)
  (x − 3)(x − 4)
  (c positive but b negative means both numbers are negative.)

sections.title: Both terms positive
sections.content:
Factorise each quadratic.

(a) x² + 5x + 6
(b) x² + 9x + 20
(c) x² + 11x + 30
(d) x² + 7x + 10

sections.title: Negative b, positive c
sections.content:
Factorise each quadratic.

(a) x² − 5x + 6
(b) x² − 8x + 15
(c) x² − 9x + 14
(d) x² − 11x + 18

sections.title: Negative c
sections.content:
Factorise each quadratic.

(a) x² + 3x − 10
(b) x² − 2x − 15
(c) x² + x − 20
(d) x² − x − 12

sections.title: Mixed factorising
sections.content:
Factorise each expression fully.

(a) x² + 4x − 21
(b) x² − 10x + 25
(c) x² − 49
(d) 3x² − 5x − 2
(e) 6x² + x − 2

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
✓ x² + 7x + 12 = (x + 3)(x + 4)
✗ x² − 5x + 6 = (x − 6)(x + 1)
✓ If c is negative, the signs in the brackets are different
✗ x² + 7x + 12 = (x + 6)(x + 2)
✓ x² − 9 = (x + 3)(x − 3) uses difference of two squares

teacher_sections.title: Teacher Key & Mark Scheme
teacher_sections.content:
Award marks for correct working and final answers.

Both terms positive:
  (a) (x + 2)(x + 3)
  (b) (x + 4)(x + 5)
  (c) (x + 5)(x + 6)
  (d) (x + 2)(x + 5)

Negative b, positive c:
  (a) (x − 2)(x − 3)
  (b) (x − 3)(x − 5)
  (c) (x − 2)(x − 7)
  (d) (x − 2)(x − 9)

Negative c:
  (a) (x + 5)(x − 2)
  (b) (x − 5)(x + 3)
  (c) (x + 5)(x − 4)
  (d) (x − 4)(x + 3)

Leading coefficient ≠ 1:
  (a) (2x + 3)(x + 1)
  (b) (3x + 1)(x + 3)
  (c) (2x + 3)(x + 2)
  (d) (5x + 1)(x + 2)

Mixed factorising:
  (a) (x + 7)(x − 3)
  (b) (x − 5)²
  (c) (x + 7)(x − 7)
  (d) (3x + 1)(x − 2)
  (e) (3x + 2)(2x − 1)
